completeness.reason: Both request obligations and the failsafe obligation are covered across explicit ownership boundaries, but the withdraw half of REQ_COOLING_REQUEST / REQ_HEATING_REQUEST is only shallowly handled - the element never says whether a withdrawal is also sent as a setpoint frame, whether it must be acknowledged, or whether it stops the running 2 s timer.
completeness.suggestion: Add the withdrawal path explicitly: how a withdrawn request is signalled to the pump/heater, whether it is acknowledgement-tracked, and what happens to an outstanding 2 s timer when the request that started it is withdrawn.

consistency.reason: Explicitly reconciled with both siblings - it never re-derives a request (ARCH_THERMAL_STATE_EVALUATOR owns the hysteresis bands) and never decides a power limit (ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR owns the 30 % fallback), and its 2 s timer matches the requirement's interval.

design_clarity.reason: Names a real mechanism (setpoint frame, acknowledgement frame correlated by request identifier, one 2 s timer per raised request) but leaves material detail unspecified: what the setpoint frame actually carries for a boolean cooling/heating request, on what bus, and whether an unacknowledged frame is retransmitted.
design_clarity.suggestion: State the setpoint frame's payload and encoding (pump speed / heater power / on-off), the transport it rides on, and whether the element retransmits on timeout or raises the unconfirmed verdict on the first expiry.

implementability.reason: Realisable as one bounded interface element, but an implementer must decide the frame payload, whether to retry, and whether a withdrawal keeps or cancels the timer - each of those changes observable behaviour.
implementability.suggestion: Resolve the retry policy and the withdrawal/timer interaction in the element text so the interface behaviour is fixed before implementation rather than chosen during it.

parent_fit.reason: Substantively owns a distinct part of each parent: it places the raised cooling/heating request on the thermal interface (REQ_COOLING_REQUEST / REQ_HEATING_REQUEST) and owns the 2 s acknowledgement timer that produces the unconfirmed verdict REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE keys on.

summary: Ownership is exemplary - the element explicitly refuses to re-derive requests or decide power limits - but the interface itself is under-specified: the setpoint frame's content, the retry/withdrawal semantics and the timer's behaviour on request withdrawal are all left open.
